payload.name: Excitement and Anticipation Event Retrieval
payload.description: When a question asks what a person is excited about, looking forward to, or anticipating (e.g., a new TV series, event, or release), include event/activity memory searches before concluding evidence is missing.
content: When the question asks what a person is excited about, looking forward to, or anticipating, do not limit the search to memory_kind=preference; the answer may be stored as an event/activity memory.

Include query variants with anticipation terms (excited about, looking forward to, upcoming, new, waiting for) together with the subject's name and the item type (e.g., TV series, movie, book, event).
If an initial preference-only search returns only general interests, run one additional hybrid or structured search with no memory_kind filter (or memory_kind=event) before answering.
Stop once a memory naming the specific upcoming item is retrieved; answer from visible evidence and do not keep expanding.

solves: Questions about what someone is excited about or looking forward to are often answered by event/activity memories (e.g., 'Tim is excited about the upcoming series X') rather than preference memories. Restricting retrieval to preference kind returns only general interests and misses the specific named item.
